utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may begin, Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The Prosecution called VG-101 to the stand. This witness has protective measures in the form of a pseudonym and facial distortion. I would like the court officer to please pass the pseudonym sheet to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Witness, you've been granted protective measures by this Court and thus we will be using a pseudonym rather than your name. Your pseudonym is number 101, Witness VG-101. On the piece of paper that's in front of you, can you confirm that -- just don't say the date, but confirm that your name and date of birth are correct on that paper in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could you also please sign this paper.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I think the witness may need a pen. And may I ask that the court officer show the pseudonym sheet to the Defence and to the Chamber, and then we will ask that it be admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the pseudonym sheet will become P93 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to ask now the court officer to provide to the witness another reference sheet.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And, Witness, this reference sheet contains the names of persons that you may be mentioning in your testimony, and next to the names there are numbers, and I'd like to ask you to please kindly refrain from mentioning any witnesses' names but, rather, refer to the sheet and to the number that is assigned to the witness. Do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And you'll receive the witness sheet in just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, this witness is a viva voce witness. We'll expect to complete her direct examination within one and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So you were saying yes with regard to the reference sheet; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Witness VG-101, in what village were you born?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I was born in the village of Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And in what municipality is Koritnik located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: The village of Koritnik is in the municipality of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And how far is the village of Koritnik from the centre of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Six kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Would you please describe for the Chamber your educational background, how many total years you went to school and what kind of school.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I attended school for 11 years, and I completed the vocational school for a worker in the tourist industry, catering.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, were the first eight years of your schooling considered to be primary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And then what was the next three years called?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: High school, except that it lasted for three years.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Muslim, Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, would you look at the sheet in front of you, and I'm going to ask you is Witness number VG-78, is this your sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, that is my sister.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And, Witness, could you please describe the ethnic mix of the Koritnik community prior to the war.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Before the war the population was mixed. There were both Muslims and Serbs living together as neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you give me the approximate percentages, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Excuse me, I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I was just asking if you knew the percentage between Serbs and Muslim residents, if it was 50 per cent and 50 per cent, or if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: There were less Muslim people. There were more Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And before the war began, were there any conflicts between the Serb residents and the Muslim residents of Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No, no conflicts.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you describe what kind of relationship the two groups shared, if any?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: The relationship was always a good one. We socialised, lived next to each other, visited each other.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, at this point in time I would like to direct your attention to the 13th day of June in 1992 and ask do you recall that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I will never forget it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And on the 13th what, if anything, occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. A neighbour of us, Djuric, Radomir, came and said that we had to leave the village, that the army was coming over from Prelovo and that they could no longer protect us. He told us that by that time they had gone through other villages burning houses and expelling people. He told us that we should join a convoy that was to go to Visegrad on the 14th of that month.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And when he said the army was coming, which army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: The Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And when he told -- you say, "He told us we should join a convoy." Could you tell us who "us" is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: He said that a convoy was to be organised with six buses from Visegrad and that we were to join the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And again when you say "we," do you mean -- please tell us who "we" is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: The Muslims from Koritnik. He said that we all had to leave to join the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us how far away Prelovo is from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Five or six kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, you were told this on the 13th. Did you at some point depart Koritnik as suggested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And when did you do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: He said that we were to go to Greben on the 14th of June and that a bus was to arrive to pick us up at 8.00 that day. We all arrived in Greben.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So you left Koritnik on -- before 8.00 in the morning on the 14th of June.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And when -- you expected to be picked up by buses in Greben. Do you know where your final destination was supposed to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: We were told that we were to go to Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And do you know what Kladanj is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I know it is a town, but I don't know where it is exactly. I've never been there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you know if it was occupied by Muslims or Serbs, or both?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I don't know. They said that we were to go to Kladanj and that the Serbs from Kladanj were to come to our houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So when you left Koritnik early in the morning on the 14th of June, how long did it take you to walk to Greben?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Half an hour on foot, because Greben is not far away from Koritnik. We arrived on time, even before 8.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber how many -- approximately how many people were in your group and tell us if you remember the types of people, men, women, children, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. I think that there were 48 or 50 of us. There were children, including a three-day-old baby, some children between 3 and 15 years of age. There were girls, men, and women.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you tell us were all of the people in the group of Muslim -- Bosnian Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. They were all Muslims, and we all hailed from the same family. We share the same last name.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Were any of the people in your group dressed in Bosnian army clothing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. We were all in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And were any people in your group armed with any type of weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No, nothing of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived in Greben, was there a bus waiting for your group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No, there was no bus. Radomir told us that he will wait with us for the bus, but in the end he didn't turn up in Greben at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So what did you and the group do next since you were in Greben and there was no bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: We waited for the bus. We spent quite some time there, although I don't know how long exactly. In any case, we were there for a considerable length of time in Greben.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, did the people in the group -- were they carrying anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. We had a lot of things with us, clothing, luggage, bags, and it was slowing us down. The things were heavy and we couldn't carry them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So after you were in Greben for a considerable length of time, then where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Then we went to -- towards Visegrad, arriving in a place called Sase. We also spent a lot of time there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And how long did it take you to get to Sase?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Another half an hour, I'd say. It is not too far away from Greben.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, in Sase did anything happen or did you see any other persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. There were many soldiers there in camouflage uniforms, sporting weapons, passing next to us. Then a Serb told us that we should go to Visegrad and that we could no longer stay there. He told us that we should go on so that we would reach Visegrad before it gets dark.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of this Serb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No, I cannot recall what his name was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And when you say there were many soldiers there in camouflage uniforms, are you talking about Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. These were all Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So then you continued your trek from Sase to Visegrad; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. We all went towards Visegrad. The Serb who told us to go said that he will go first at the head of the column in his vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting, but I have a feeling that the last two questions were leading questions, just to remind the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: "And when you say there were many soldiers there in camouflage, are you talking about Serbs?"

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That is leading, so the answer is useless.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I will rephrase the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I need to ask you a question again. When you referred to soldiers that were in camouflage uniforms --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the mike is on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us where those soldiers were from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I can't. I don't know where they were from. They were just there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you know what country they were from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: They were from the same country as myself. These were local Serbs, the local Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And they were -- what colour was the camouflage uniforms they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: They wore camouflage uniforms, olive-drab in colour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, when you left -- did you leave Sase at some point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. We went towards Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And did you eventually reach Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: We arrived in Visegrad, although I don't know at what time exactly. In the end we did arrive there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, between your trek from Koritnik to Visegrad, did you ever see any buses driving along the road on which you were walking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: There was one bus that passed by us in Sase, and there were people from the village of Vlahovici on it. It passed by on the read in the direction of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you tell us what kind of bus this was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: It was a Centrotrans Transport Company bus.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, did you know -- did you see anyone or did you know anyone who was on board of this bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. It just passed by in the direction of Visegrad. It did not stop there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived in Visegrad what -- where did your group go first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: We went down the main street in Visegrad. Some Serb policemen and Serb soldiers were in front of the MUP building. They told us to take Jondza Street next to the Drina in order to reach the Red Cross building.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Chamber the Serb policemen and Serb soldiers that you saw, in particular what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: The Serb policemen had blue camouflage uniforms. The rest had camouflage uniforms of another colour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did anyone in your group speak with any of the policemen or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. They just kept screaming at us, telling us that we should go down Jondza Street in order to get to the Red Cross building.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I know it's been a long time, but can you remember any of the words or anything -- any -- anything that they were saying to you in particular, other than to go to the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. They told us to go to the Red Cross building. We took the street, but the building was closed since it was a Sunday. In front of the new hotel there were other policemen and other Serbs in camouflage uniforms. They lined us up in pairs, insulting us, provoking us, yelling at us. From the village a dog accompanied us, and it was killed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I want to just stop you for a minute. You said the Red Cross was closed. So I think you're jumping ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, it was a Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Where did you go after you discovered that the Red Cross was closed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: From the Red Cross building we arrived in front of the new hotel building. We stopped in front of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And then you just described some events that were going on. Can you give us that description again in more detail, what you remember happened, if anything, to you at the Novi Hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: This Serb policeman lined us up in pairs. They provoked us, yelling at us. There was a dog that accompanied us from the village. They killed it, and they forced a man that was with us to throw the corpse off the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And when they did these things to you, were you standing outside of the hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. We were in front of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And at any point in time did you or anyone in the group go inside the hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. They put us in the hotel garden next to the bridge so that we would no longer stand in the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And as they were provoking and yelling at you, did you hear them talking amongst themselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Were any of these men armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, at some point did something else happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. They were discussing among themselves where to put us, whether in the garden or to go to Bikavac. During that time -- and a Serb arrived who told them to send us off to the neighbourhood where there was some abandoned Muslim houses.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The witness mentioned the name of the Serbian person, but we failed to pick that up.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could you tell us, if you know, the name of the neighbourhood where they were talking about, that they were talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: It was Mitar Vasiljevic who told us to go to Mahala to Pionirska Street to the abandoned Muslim houses there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And are you -- were you familiar with the Mahala settlement on Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And how were you familiar with this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I knew about it because some of my village relatives lived there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So did the group then embark off for -- towards Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. We were in a column in pairs. They told us to go down the main street in Visegrad towards Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And when you got to Mahala, what street were you on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And how long did it take? Approximately how long did it take you to walk to Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Perhaps 15 to 20 minutes. Not much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And when you got to Pionirska Street, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: When we arrived there a female relative of mine was there in a house with her under-aged son and mother-in-law. She came out and said that she could not take us in, that there were too many of us and that we should go to some of the other houses. Mitar Vasiljevic followed us, gathered us around him and he said we can no longer live together. "You are to go to Kladanj, to the Muslim houses there, and the people from there will go to your houses." He told us that we should all enter a house that was there at that point.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: After Mitar Vasiljevic said this to you, then what happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: We all entered the house. It was he who showed us which house to go to. He was present. We all entered the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, this -- just so the record's clear, you said that he told you all to go to Kladanj, but you were still on Pionirska Street at this time when you entered a house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. He told us that we were to leave the next morning early on the 15th of June at 6.00. He said that we were late for the buses that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you know whose house your group was occupying at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I think the person's name was Ragib.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, this Mitar Vasiljevic person, could you please tell us what he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: He was wearing an olive-drab uniform, a long black overcoat, and a black hat.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And did you know him prior to this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: From the times when I attended school in Prelovo. He resided there, and I saw him there often.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did you see him anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. He worked in Visegrad as a waiter in a hotel. I don't know which one exactly. That is where I occasionally saw him as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So when you saw him at this time on the 14th of June, did you recognise him or did you learn his identity through his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. I recognised him immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, when you got into this house, did Mitar Vasiljevic stay or did he leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: He left.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did he say anything else to any of the occupants in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. He gave a piece of paper to a man that was with us, some sort of an assurance that no one should touch us. He told us that if Serbian police arrive that we should show them our IDs. He also said that we were first to be put on the buses the next morning to leave for Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And at some point did Mitar Vasiljevic leave the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And then what did the group do at this point when you were inside the house? Was everyone in one room? Can you please describe what it was like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. We enter the house. We were drenched from the brain that had been falling the whole day. We changed out of the wet clothes and sat in the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, at some point in time did anyone else come to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. As we were sitting in the house Milan Lukic entered the room where I was. He was the first one. He kicked open the door with his boot and was followed by three more Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you tell us approximately what time this was, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I don't know precisely, but it was around 5.00 or 6.00 p.m. He came right after Mitar Vasiljevic. I think less than half an hour had elapsed before their arrival.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you know if Milan Lukic and three -- the other three persons you describe as Serbs, if they arrived in any vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't hear a vehicle stop. It was the main road, and the vehicles passed constantly. I saw them first as the door was kicked open, but I don't know if they arrived in a car.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, before I ask you some questions about Mr. Lukic, I would like to ask you if you can tell us -- describe the other three persons whom you've said were Serbs, describe for the Judges.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The other Serb was somewhat short than Milan Lukic. He sported a black moustache and had black curly hair. The other Serb had blonde or light brown hair. He was a bit taller and of somewhat heavier built than Lukic, and a third one seemed the youngest among them. He was 18 or perhaps even younger. He was tall, gangly, and the youngest of the group.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did any of these four men disguise their faces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. Their faces were clearly to be seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And how many of these men did you recognise when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I recognised Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, I would like to ask you some questions about how it was you were able to recognise Milan Lukic. Did you know him from before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. I had known him very well. We went together to the primary school in Prelovo. He was only a year older. We went together to the secondary school as well. We didn't go to the same class. We were in part of the same class, but we went to the same school. So I had known him for a number of years.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: You went to school for 11 years; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did you see him often during these 11 years that you were in school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. I'd see him every day in the hallways and on the school grounds. I'd always come across him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, did you -- what age were you when you finished secondary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I was 18.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And how old were you in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I was 23.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, did you see Milan Lukic between your age of 18 and 23?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And where would you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I saw him round the town. I'd see him in the village of Prelovo where dances or parties were organised and attended by Muslims and Serbs alike. That's where I'd see him, because both Serbs and Muslims would attend these balls or dances.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, between the time you were in school to 1992 did you notice whether his appearance changed and, if so, in what way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. Perhaps slightly. He may have grown stouter, but the face remained quite the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, I'll take you back to the house on Pionirska Street. When these men entered the room, what did they say? What did -- did any of them say anything and, if so, whom and what did that person say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. They placed a bag on the table and said, "Money, gold, place all of it on the table. If we find anything on anyone, we will kill you all."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you recall who said that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Milan Lukic did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, did you hear these four men speaking with each other, calling each other any type of names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did you hear them speaking to any of the other occupants in the house and using their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I may have asked you this and I apologise, but were you all in one room or several rooms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. There was a living-room. There was another room or perhaps two more rooms and a hallway. We couldn't all fit into one room, and people were split among the three rooms or between the two or three rooms. I don't know how many there were.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, after Milan Lukic said, "Money, gold, place all of it on the table, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: We gave whatever we had. We turned it over, the money, the gold. There were even foreign currency banknotes, Deutschmarks and Austrian shillings and -- so that Milan even commented upon that fact by saying something to the effect, "Oh, we even have foreign currency banknotes here."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And what about your jewellery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. Whatever we had, we placed in the bag.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, after this happened or while this was happening, did anything else happen? Did these -- did anything else happen? Did these men order -- okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. When they were finished with the looting, then the moustached Serb with black curly hair started separating women by ones or by twos. We were supposed to go over to the next room with him and take all of our clothes off.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: He said that we should come along with him for an examination, that we should take our clothes off in order for him to make sure and see clearly that we had not withheld any of the money or jewellery.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And where was Milan Lukic while this was being -- the searches were being conducted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: They were on the staircase leading to the front door of the house. That's where they stood while he was searching us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. I need to clarify. You say, "They were on the staircase leading to the front door of the house. That's where they stood while he was searching us." Now, who was searching you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: We were being searched by the moustached Serb with curly hair.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And does "they" refer to the other three men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. They were there in the house. Whether they were on the staircase or in another room while he was searching us. And as he searched some of the women, he instructed us to go to a specific room after having been searched so that he might keep track of the women he had searched and the ones he had not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And when you're using the pronoun "he," you're referring to the man with the moustache?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So do you know if all the women in that group were searched?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, all of them. He wasn't looking for money at all. This was just a way for him to humiliate us as much as he could. He only wanted us to strip naked. He didn't even bother to go through the clothing to look for what he was purportedly looking for. He was sitting on a chair laughing at us while we were forced to appear naked before him. That was terrible humiliation for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you tell me approximately how long these strip searches took?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: It went on for quite a long time. There were quite a few of us women and girls. It took some time for us to take our clothes off and then put them back on. So it did take quite a while.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did you see -- at any point did you see Milan Lukic in the room where women were being searched?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. Only the moustached Serb was in that room, and he was the only one searching us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you know if there were searches going on in other rooms of which you didn't have any visibility for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: We all had to appear before him in that room. All the women had to.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So what happened -- excuse me, another question. Do you know if any of the men were searched?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No, you don't remember, or no, they weren't?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. Only the women and girls were searched.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, after the strip searches what, if anything, happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: When he was all done with it, then the moustached Serb told Lukic, "I found a good one for you." Lukic then asked him, "What size does she wear?" I don't know what it meant. I only know that they laughed after he said that. Then they took a girl outside of the house, and they all went with her. They went away with her.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And without saying her name, did you know who this girl was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I know her very well. She was married to a relative of mine. She was 15 years old and had only been married for a year.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, after they went away with her did -- did -- eventually did she return and, if so, whom was she with when she returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. They brought her back to the house. At one point I was sitting on the ground in the kitchen and there were quite a few women around me. Milan Lukic entered the room and told me, "Get up. Are you wearing jeans?" He was able to see full well that I didn't have any jeans, but nevertheless he said, "Get up. Are you wearing any jeans?" I stood is up, and we looked each other in the eye and gazed into each other's eyes for five minutes. Then the moustached Serb came along and said, "That's not her." He got into the room and took another girl out. He brought her over to Lukic. When Lukic saw her, since he had known her well, he said, "Well, well, who do we have here? How come you're here? What are you doing here?" He put her arm -- put his arm around her, and they all went out with the girl.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And you say you knew who the second girl was as well. You don't have to say her name, but you knew her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, I knew her well. Lukic had been taking her away before that as well. She had run away from him and had tried to hide with us in the village. That's how she came to be in our group as we set out for Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, when the first girl was brought back, did you have a chance to speak with her or see her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. I was sitting next to her. She was crying, and she told me that they had raped her. She said, "God forbid that that should happen to you." They asked her, "Why didn't you smear something on your face and then they would not have raped you." And they said, "It's not going to be just you. All of the women and girls will experience the same."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did she say which of the men told her this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Milan Lukic told her as much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, did you have a chance to -- no. After the second girl was taken out, did she return to the house as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. She returned without telling me anything. She was weeping and lay down, covered herself with a blanket and stayed silent.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, can you tell me approximately how long all of this took from the time you say Milan kicked down the door until this point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I would object to the characterisation of kicking down the door. That's a misstatement of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't think -- I don't believe the evidence was very much different, from my recollection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't say that the door was knocked down. I said that it was opened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The door was not knocked down. It was opened.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The question was approximately how much time had elapsed between the time the door was opened and this point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. We couldn't keep track of the time. We didn't have a watch on us to be able to tell the time. It was difficult to establish how much time had elapsed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you recall if it was getting dark outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: When they brought the girl back, they took away a woman who had three children. They brought her as far as the stairs, but her daughter was crying and holding, gripping her. They couldn't separate them, so they brought them back into the room.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did anything else happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Next they said that they were going somewhere to have roast of lamb and something to drink and warned us that we should all stay indoors. As they left the house, it started to get dark.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, who said that they were going somewhere to roast of lamb and something to drink?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Milan Lukic said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, when you say you were all warned to stay indoors, can you recall exactly what was said to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. They said that nobody should leave the house, that we all had to stay indoors. We weren't even allowed to come out the front door. We all had to stay in the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And when you say "they," again could you please identify the speaker if you're able to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Milan Lukic and the other Serbs who were with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did any of the men state that they would be back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. They said, "We'll be back, and when we come back," that's something that they told the victim that they raped, "we don't have the time now, but everybody will get their turn."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's another leading question, you know, Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'll restate the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we have the answer already, but "Did any of them state that they will be back," which is I imagine a point of issue, but you told the witness the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, my question is who said "we'll be back," if anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. All of them said that they would be back.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And the victim that they raped, you stated that she said something one of them had said. Did you tell you which one had said that to her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Milan Lukic said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: How were you feeling at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Horrible. I wouldn't wish it upon anyone to feel that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, after the men left the house --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I can understand that, Ms. Sartorio, stated that she said something one of them had said and said Milan Lukic said that, but what is it he said?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Line 23 -- excuse me, page 23, line 24 -- or 25. "Yes, they --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Oh, I see. It's the same issue of being back.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, at that -- no. At that point, Your Honour, she's talking about something -- something they told the victim that they raped. "We don't have the time now, but everybody will get their turn." My question was: "Did the victim tell you, Witness, who said that to her?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. She told me that it was Milan Lukic who had told her that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, I asked you how you were feeling. Did you talk to any of the other people in the house after the men left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: We talked to each other, but we stayed silent rather than talking.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did anyone talk about who these men were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. A man was saying -- they were all saying that they knew them. We all knew who those men were and what they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you tell us who -- when you say, "We all knew who those men were and what they were," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Well, we already knew by that time what the Serbian army was doing to the Muslim people around Visegrad. It was all very clear to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. I'm talking about these specific four men, whether anyone in the room discussed who they were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, at some point in the evening did anything else happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know what time it was. It may have been at around 11.00 or 12.00 p.m. A car -- or rather, 12.00 a.m. A car pulled over in front of the house. It was quite noisy, the engine of the car. They flashed the lights at the windows and at the front door of the house and told us to get out of that house and move over to another house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, let's just take it a little bit slower. When you say a car pulled over in front of the house, did you actually see this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I didn't see that, but I heard the car. Some of the people who were by the window could see the car out in the street quite clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And were the people in front of the window say anything about who was in the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. They weren't able to see who was in the car.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And then after the car arrived what was the next thing that happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: They said that we should come out of that house and move over to a different house. They told us that we needn't bother to put our shoes on. We could go barefoot because we were only changing houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, when you say, "They said we should come out of the house," who is "they," please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. The Serbs who arrived said that. In the doorway there was that same moustached -- moustached Serb who shone his flashlight torch toward the interior of the house and told us that we should get out of the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So that's the first person you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. He was outside the front door of that house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So then what did you and the group do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: The people were panic-stricken for a moment. There was commotion in the house. Some moved to fetch their belongings, although we were told not to take any belongings with us. At one point I got out onto the balcony because I was entertaining the idea of jumping out of the balcony. I wanted to avoid facing them at any cost. However, the house was too big. It was two floors up, and I didn't dare to jump, so I got out of the house with the others.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, so far you've seen the man with the moustache at the door. Did you hear any of the other -- any other persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. Not right there outside the front door, and that's where he was. For a brief moment I saw Mitar Vasiljevic behind him. I put my boots on, and it took me quite a while to get my boots on, and by the time I did only the man with the moustache was standing outside the door, and he was standing there all that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: At some point in time did you exit that first house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. I went out. He pointed in a certain direction and said, "Go down that way." In front of me at some distance I could see a blonde Serb whom I described. He stood there with a large torchlight lighting the road we were to take. He was also shedding some light on us, and one could see well the whole area. He said that we should go towards that man who was down the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Just so -- again so the record is clear, at the beginning of your answer you said, "He pointed in a certain direction." Are you talking about the man with the moustache at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. He said, "Go down there," where the blonde Serb was and where there was light. He held a torchlight lighting our way as we were approaching him from the direct of the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And I'm going to show you a photograph in just a moment, Witness, so you can identify where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting. Just one technical I think error in the transcript. Page 27, line 15. I think that it was the answer, not the question. Just for clarification of transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, did you recognise the person whom you describe as the blonde Serb holding the light?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. It was the same person who came to the house with Lukic as they were looting and taking money and jewellery away from us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And -- so what happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I went in that direction. Some people were in front of me. I was halfway there, and I knew that if I were to go into the light, to the blonde man, that there was no way I would survive. I never feared death, and I didn't run away. The only thing I was afraid of was rape. I thought that if I went down there that they would separate the women and girls, as they had before. I turned back to the house and looked at the Serb who was in front of the door, the one with the moustache. He noticed me hesitating and then made a few steps in my direction. I turned around again and went the same way. The blonde Serb shed some light on me, and as he was putting the torchlight down, his eyes went down as well. I made use of that moment, and I ran to the left some ten metres, and I hid behind a shed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Let me stop you there, please. Thank you. Now, before you used that moment to run to the left, did you see what was going on in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. I saw the people coming near the blonde Serb entering that -- the other house. There was a girl standing next to him. She had some medical problems and was not attending school. She probably did not understand where she was supposed to go, and she just kept standing there looking at him. The others in front of me were all entering the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, other than the blonde man did you see anyone else that was not part of your group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Sorry, I did not understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: You saw the man with the moustache, and then you saw the blonde man. Did you see anyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I saw Milan Lukic and Mitar Vasiljevic standing in front of the house where the people were going into. They were in the lit area. They were looking at the house at the moment when I ran for the shed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point I would like the court officer to please bring up Exhibit P77. It's a photograph. Is that as large as we can make it? Okay. And perhaps to assist the witness. I'm going to ask her to make some markings on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Witness 101, have you seen this photograph before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'd like you to make some markings for me and I'm going to ask you, first, do you see Pionirska Street on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could you please draw a line along the street and put a P for Pionirska, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, do you see in this photograph the first house that you and the group were in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could you put a 1 on the roof of that house, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, do you -- if you recall where the door was on that house approximately, could you put a V for door in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So was the door actually -- it's on the -- it fronts that little street or paved little alley; correct? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you please label the second house which you said people were walking into before you escaped from the group and put a 2.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And if you know where the door of that house was could you label that with 2V -- or a V is fine, if you recall.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, can you also identify in this photograph the shed that you ran to, if you're able, and put an S on it, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now I'd like you to draw, if you would, a line with an arrow at the end for the -- where the people walked from the first house to the second house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, can you draw a circle at the point where you left the group and ran for the shed. Just put a dot.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, could you also tell us approximately where the man with the moustache -- you want to make a correction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can we erase the first one then? Now, can you show us in this photograph where the man with the moustache was standing as you were leaving the house, approximately? And I'd like you to mark that with an M -- M1 for Man 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: M1 or just 1?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: What did you put down there? It's a little confusing now. Can we mark the door again, start over with the door and then where the man with the moustache -- could you mark a V for the door.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And I think it might be easier to put an X for the man with the moustache. I'm going to ask you to use a different colour pen at this point and put an X.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Just for the record the markings thus far have been in blue and now we're using red.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So the X is where the man with the moustache was standing. Now, can you mark an X2 where the second -- the man, the blonde man with the flashlight was standing. Red, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And now could you mark an ML where you saw Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Which letters?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: ML for his -- his name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And was Mitar -- where was Mitar Vasiljevic in relation to Milan Lukic? You can put an MV.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, do we have another colour, a green perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And while we're waiting for that, was there light coming from any of the houses, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Are we green at this -- could you put an X at the houses -- or house where you saw light coming from.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And you drew an arrow for the -- is that for the direction where the light was shining?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. This area was all lit up.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of device it was that was lighting up this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: There were torchlights around. As for the light from the house, maybe there were some bulbs there, but it was a proper light.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And now before we mark and enter this as an exhibit, can you indicate for us on this map where -- what direction you went? Did you eventually leave the shed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: How long were you in the shed before you left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: We were there for a brief period of time, five to ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And using the green marker, which is fine, could you indicate the route that you took after you left the shed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask that this photograph be marked as an exhibit in evidence, entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will become Exhibit P94, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, after you left the shed, approximately how long did you travel to somewhere, and what was your final destination?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: We followed the creek for a while and then crossed over to the right side. There were large garden fences there, tall fences. Having crossed that, we entered a forest.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, were you with anyone at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. My sister was with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Who had followed me behind the shed. It was myself and my sister.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you were -- were running at this point or moving -- how fast were you moving from the shed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. We moved quickly to flee as quickly as we could, to get as far as possible. However, we didn't know which way to turn. We couldn't go anywhere. They were everywhere in Visegrad. We wanted to reach the forest, feeling it was the safest place. It didn't matter to us much what would happen in the forest, whether we would die or kill ourselves. We were just desperately trying to reach the forest.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, as you were running away from the shed did you hear anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: When we entered the shed, we heard shots coming from the house next to the creek. I remember telling my sister, "These people are killing our mother, our mother-in-law, and our brother's two children. They didn't do anything wrong." It hurt so much I wouldn't wish anyone to experience that. It was horrific.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: At this time, Your Honours, let me bring up Exhibit P90. And this will be my last few questions, or do you want to take a break?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. That is fine. Let us go on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: In line 21 it should be sister-in-law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So we have another Judge, but I think we'll take the break now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'm almost finished. Perhaps five minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Let's finish.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Exhibit P90, please. This will be under seal. It is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, Witness, looking at this exhibit that is before you, are you able to read this document and, if so, can you tell me what it is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And what is this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: These are the names of people who were killed in the house, the names of my family members, relatives who were killed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And these are the people that were part of the group that left Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. These are all the people I had arrived with from the village and with whom I was in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, if you could move the first page up a little bit. I'm going to ask you if on this list -- have you seen any of the people on this list since the 14th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And if you're going to mention them, could you please mention their pseudonyms if it applies.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Very well. All right. I have seen four people who survived the burning of the house. It is VG-085, VG-013, VG-038, and VG-078. It is my sister. As well as VG-018.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The first pseudonym is VG-084.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And are you aware of anyone who has seen any of the other persons named on this list since the 14th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. Two other men survived the house; however, they are no longer among the living. They died their natural deaths.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: One more question. Witness, at this time I would like you to take a look around the courtroom, please, and look at everyone, and other than myself and Mr. Stewart, Esq and Mr. Groome, Esq, ask you if you recognise anyone in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, usual objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's noted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And we would join as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Take your time and look at everyone.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. I don't need any additional time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Who do you recognise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I know Milan Lukic. I recognise him. He is sitting there next to the first person to the left.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And just so it's more clear, do you see two men on either --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask -- I think he's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I was afraid -- I apologise for my fast reaction. I was afraid that something will be leading in this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I just want -- it won't be.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, on the -- do you see four men sitting up in that second row?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I see four men.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And the two men on the outside on each side, they're wearing blue shirts. Do you see those men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, I do. They are not the ones. Milan Lukic is wearing a white shirt. He has a headset, and he's writing something just now. That is Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Is he the man wearing glasses or is he not wearing glasses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No, he is not wearing glasses.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Are you able to see the colour of his tie, Milan Lukic's tie?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I can't see his tie. He is bending forward. I cannot see any tie.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the record reflect that the witness has identified Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: One last question. Witness 101, is this the man who you saw at the house on Pionirska Street on the 14th of June and who was outside --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, no. I don't think that's leading. She's just identifying the context.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the man.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So this is Mr. Alarid now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. VG-101.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I apologise that I can't speak to you by your proper name. It seems disrespectful to use these numbers but we have to do this to protect everyone's identity, and so I hope you understand that I don't mean any disrespect by calling you VG-101.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Briefly, Your Honour, I would like to go into private session. I'm going to mention a couple names, and I don't have a pseudonym sheet prepared, and so could we go into private session briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could the court assistant please bring up the marked photo P94.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, looking at the photograph, ma'am, I'd like you to focus on the -- the roof that you marked with a green X and also with a blue S. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, isn't it true that this is a single building, a single shed that is hidden by a tree that has grown --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So it is two --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. These are two smaller structures. It's a shed -- the shed where I ran to and another building that was lit up. So these are two small buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, the home that you wrote a number 1 on, isn't it true there was no electricity in that home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, there was no electricity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that the roof that you've marked with a green X is not a home, it is just another shed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. It resembled a shed. It was a roofed-in structure that was opened on one side. It may have been a shed or a garage. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And if there was no electricity in the house at number 1, highly likely there was no electricity in that garage or shed. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: There was electricity there, and the entire area was lit up. I don't know where the light came from, but it was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So lit up by like floodlights?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: It seemed as if the entire area had been lit up by way of bulbs that were somewhere there. Plus they had the torches with them. So the entire area was lit up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But a torch is an interesting kind of light, because it only lights up where the torch is pointed. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. They used the torches on our way from the large house to where it is marked in blue, because that large house was quite dark, and they wanted us to come out in the lit-up area where they could clearly see us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, was there floodlights or buildings lit up anywhere else other than this garage or shed and the torchlights from the assailants?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, because there were Serb homes on Pionirska Street, and some of the light came from those homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But they're on the other side and off the photograph, not in view. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I don't exactly know where they are. I only know that we could see the light from those houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the lights would be just coming out of ordinary windows, bedrooms and what-not and would not have -- would not have flooded the area with light but merely been in the house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. The usual lighting in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when you were leaving the home, being told to go to the number 2 house, how many people had left before you, because you indicated you had to put your boots on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. I put my boots on. I don't know how many had left before me, but I know that quite a few had and had already gone to the other house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when you say they'd already gone to the other house, would it be fair to say that if they were even gone to the other house they weren't all inside? You weren't walking by yourselves across this open area. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. They were reaching the blonde Serb who was in the lit-up area. They first reached him and then proceeded to enter the second house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And those people would have been in between you and the people that you noted as ML and MV. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: They went ahead of me and reached the lit-up area where the blonde Serb was. At the time, I was halfway there. They, on the other hand, reached the Serb who stood in that lit-up area.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the other people that were in this procession, they helped block the view of your escape. Wouldn't that be true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. No, they didn't block me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm not saying block you. I'm saying they blocked, let's say, the blonde Serb from seeing that you were -- and your sister were able to escape.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: They couldn't block my view because they didn't linger there by his side. They immediately proceeded on to the other house. As they reached the man, they went past him and on. They wouldn't stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But this was a procession of 70 people, so that procession went on for quite some time. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. But we did not all come out of the house in a group. We went by twos or in single file. There wasn't a crowd of people in one small space. We did not obstruct each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that they were everywhere. I'm assuming these soldiers. What do you mean "they were everywhere," as you were headed towards the shed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. I meant the Serb soldiers, that they were everywhere, in the surrounding streets, on Pionirska Street, in Visegrad in general. Even a check-point, a barricade, was placed at the end of Pionirska Street toward the Rodica hill. They wanted to obstruct free movement there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was this -- was this barricade there earlier in the day when you proceeded to the Mahala neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So it appears that the barricade was set up to maybe prevent people from escaping down Pionirska Street if other people knew about this tragedy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Because two women tried to go to their family's home, and they tried to -- they told them that they couldn't go over there and told them to head back.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And this was between the time when you had arrived at Pionirska Street but before it had got dark or when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: This was at the outset. They wanted to see their homes but weren't able to get past that point, and they came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And again was that before it got dark and after you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. Before it got dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so people in the homes were able to leave the homes? There was no guards left all day after Mr. Vasiljevic told the people to go there and gave that one gentleman a piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. We weren't able to go down the street because barricades had been erected. Had we been able to pass through, we would have gone to the houses of our relatives there, but we weren't able to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So the soldiers had set up barricades after you had been led to Pionirska.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I don't know when it was exactly that they were erected. The barricades may have been there from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, you didn't notice them walking into the neighbourhood. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when you went to the shed, you went with your sister or did you go with anybody else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I didn't go into the shed. I went behind the shed. My sister was following behind without me noticing that. As soon as I slipped away behind the shed, I heard her moving behind me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that your sister stayed close by you that whole day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, at these barricades, were the soldiers there police or military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't go. Two other women did and saw that. I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did they mention whether or not they were police or military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that there were soldiers everywhere. Can you estimate how many soldiers were in town and in and around the Pionirska Street neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't possibly know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I don't -- I'm not trying to get you to name an exact number, but maybe give me a round number like more than a hundred, more than 500, or whatever you might think.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. I don't want to speculate, and I don't know the exact number. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
