utterances.text: Now, you did see both police and military in town as you were coming in. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you saw most of the police in the square when you first arrived and at the hotel. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. In front of the SUP too. That's where the police headquarters was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, after you were able to escape behind the shed following the green line, you're saying that you went down into the creek bottom and moved up? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I look at this photograph that you've marked on, and it appears that the vegetation, the trees and the bushes and the creek are very thick and might have been able to hide your presence down there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. I wasn't hiding there. I didn't want to stay there for another five minutes. I wanted to get away from the place as soon as may be.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You misunderstood me. What I meant by that was is that the vegetation would help conceal you as you made your way up the creek.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. We couldn't be spotted because it was dark. It was night-time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so the bottom of the creek was not lit up by any lights. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No, no. It was dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And on direct examination the Prosecution -- or you testified that you first started hearing shots when you were still behind the shed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No, that's not true. I said that I heard the first shots when I got into the forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Understood. Okay. I misunderstood you. Now, you're saying you saw Mitar Vasiljevic in front of the house. Are you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Are you certain you're not mistaken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, isn't it true that you'd not seen him there since earlier in the afternoon when he gave the piece of paper to Muho?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I saw him in the evening, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that was before it got dark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: In the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you hear that Mitar Vasiljevic broke his leg on the 14th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If he broke his leg at 5.00 in the afternoon, is it possible that you're mistaken about seeing him later in the evening, around midnight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I was not mistaken, and he did not break his leg. That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: He never broke his leg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. Well, I don't know. Maybe he did at some point, but he definitely did not on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If he broke -- brought in a lot of medical records and doctors and X-rays --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: -- would that change your mind?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Again he's asking if a witness brought in medical records. He could -- that's not a proper question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It would not change your mind?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, the same -- I object to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just explain the basis for the objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The basis for the objection is it's not -- if he brought in a lot of medical records and doctors and X-rays, and what he's getting at is again what he's been doing in the past, which is putting -- putting another witness's statement or what another witness might do before this witness and asking this witness to draw an opinion as to whether if a witness did that it would change her mind. He can put the proposition to the witness that if there were medical records -- hold on one moment. I'm sorry, Your Honour. The basis of the objection is that there's no -- there's no evidence that there were any medical records here, in her testimony or anywhere in the trial for this witness, and he's drawing information out of thin air and putting it to the witness as a hypothetical question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I agree, Mr. Alarid. It really invites speculation more than anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I guess one of the reasons I think it's somewhat relevant is because this witness has testified in the Mitar Vasiljevic case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I have ruled, so please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when you did run from area and you ran left to the back of the shed, I'm assuming you covered that ground very, very quickly, as quick as you could.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And once you were behind something that blocked your view, both of them and you, I'm sure you wanted to stay hidden. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Before I hurled myself to the side I was standing right there and was able to take in fully what was taking place around me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The question I asked you, ma'am, is when you hurled yourself to the side, you probably made that movement very quickly. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when you got -- and when you got behind the shed you wanted to stay hidden and, of course, not be seen by anyone else.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. I was lying behind the shed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the extra microphones please be switched off.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when you -- how far away was this wooded area that you heard the first shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. We followed the creek but not for long, and then went alongside garden fences before we reached the forest. It wasn't that far off.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was it more than a hundred metres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did the shooting seem distant? Something to help you put it in perspective.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. It seemed close.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to describe what everyone was wearing. Can you do that? What was the man in the moustache wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: They had camouflage uniforms on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what was the primary colour of the camouflage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: The camouflage uniforms had a mixture of yellow and brown.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was the man with the moustache wearing anything on his head?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was he armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the man that you say was Mitar Vasiljevic, how was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: He had an olive-grey uniform and a black overcoat reaching all the way to the ground and a black hat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, it had been raining earlier and he was wearing that overcoat because of the rain. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I don't know, and I'm not particularly interested in why he was wearing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please don't ask questions like that. As you know, the witness can't answer them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You were all wet because of walking in the rain that day. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. It rained the whole night and the whole day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was it still raining at midnight when you were able to get away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, it was, the whole night. As I was fleeing with my sister through the forest, it rained throughout the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And was it actually raining while people were moving from one house to another?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when the people were first told to move from one house to the other you said that there was panic and confusion, and you went to see if you could jump off a balcony. Were you upstairs or downstairs when the men first came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: We were on the floor of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The first floor, ma'am, or the second floor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: The second floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so you were up there -- were you asleep when they first arrived or were you awake?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No, we were not asleep. We were awake.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, the moment it got dark in that house, I'm assuming that there was no light, and between that time no one came back after dark, between midnight and earlier in the day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Excuse me. I did not understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It was a bad question. I apologise. There was no electricity in the house; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: There was no electricity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I'm assuming -- what time did it get dark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: It started getting dark around 6.00 or 7.00. I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And between the time it got dark and the time the men came to move the people, had any one of those men come back in the middle, after dark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. They came to tell us to move from one house to the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And before that time and in between when it got dark, did anyone come back to the house for any reason?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Excuse me, could you please repeat? I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Between the time when the men came and asked people to move from one house to another and the time it got dark, did anyone come back to the house? Basically, after dark did anyone come back until you were moved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Before it got dark is when they came, and just as it was starting to get dark they left. The next time they returned it was already dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that's at the end when they asked people to move?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. They came once we arrived in the house. Lukic was there with another three Serbs right after we got into the house, both before it was dark and after.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when the car grow up -- drove up, you heard that it was -- you heard it because it was very loud?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Had this car -- had this loud noise -- had you heard it before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you remember what kind of car it was? Did you ever see it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: At the end of the night was there more than four Serbs at the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: There were four Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that's it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Sorry, the big house?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When you were asked as a group to move from the big house to the other house, there was just the four Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: In front of the big house and the other house I could see four people. Other victims saw -- I don't know. I saw four.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that's all you ever saw that evening was four?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honours. Asked and answered several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Move on, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Avoid comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did I make a comment, Your Honour? I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I believe the question was in the form of a comment. That's my interpretation of it. So just move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in your direct examination a little bit earlier, you stated that, "We all know who those men were and what they were. We knew what the Serbian army was doing." What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: We knew what they had been doing, that they were killing Muslims, expelling them from towns and other villages. The -- we knew they had the power in their hands as well as the weapons, that they could do with the Muslims whatever they wanted to and they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Before that date had you heard stories and rumours about Milan Lukic or Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. A man from the group spoke with Mitar and knew him well. There was another woman who spoke with Mitar as well. He told her about her brother, Osman Kurspahic. He told her that he was taken away and transferred to Sarajevo to safe territory. He also said that we will get to Kladanj and that she could see for herself that her brother was still alive. However, things did not go in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was Mitar Vasiljevic armed that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When you first saw him in the daylight was he armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, during the time in the house from when you first got there in the afternoon all the way into the evening, did your sister stay with you the whole time or did you get separated at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. We were together all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that none of the men in the house used names with each other to identify each other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: They may have been using names, but I didn't hear them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You didn't hear anyone come in and introduce themselves as if ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that you knew Milan Lukic because you went to school with him. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. I knew him very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you were a grade behind him. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But would it be fair to say that you hadn't seen him since secondary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I didn't see him frequently, but I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, can you recall the last time you would have seen Milan Lukic in town before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And if we could use April of 1992 as when the war started, when was the first time you had seen Milan Lukic or who you believed to be Milan Lukic after the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I saw him on the 14th of June in Visegrad, in Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so going backwards in time, can you recall the circumstances that would have been the last time you saw Milan Lukic before the war?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let her answer it. Can you remember when last you saw Milan Lukic before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you indicated on direct examination that his appearance had changed perhaps slightly but the face was still the same. What kind of things had changed slightly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: While he attended school he was thinner. Later, he appeared to have gained some weight. However, the features of his face remain the same. The rest is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What about his haircut?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so when you knew him in high school he had the same haircut that he had in Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Perhaps slightly different. When he was at school, his hair was parted to one side, but at Pionirska Street it didn't appear to be the case. It was changed slightly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that Milan Lukic as a young man had long hair at all times?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when you went to school with Milan Lukic, did you guys have the same homeroom teacher as in primary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: The same teachers. There were two or three different teachers, but it's the same people.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that there are two shifts at school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, but sometimes we would be together in the first or the second shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what year did you finish your high school or secondary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I finished it in 1986.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And do you remember your homeroom teacher in high school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: In high school we didn't have a single homeroom teacher. We had different teachers. You have homeroom teachers in elementary school only.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now in primary school did you go all the time in Prelovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. The teacher's name was Dragan Simic from Prelovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And is that was from which grade to which grade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Up to the fourth grade, between the first and the fourth grade it was Dragan Simic. From the fifth up to the eighth there were different teachers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that some children from Rujiste went to different primary school for the first four years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. No, because the school in Prelovo was just next door basically. It was the closest school to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: To Rujiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. Rujiste is close to Prelovo. The school was almost at their doorstep. Rujiste is close to Prelovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How far is the primary school Prelovo to your village in Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Five or six kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how far -- what about Klasnik? Was there a school in Klasnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I don't remember. If there was one, it was for the children of Klasnik, not for the children of Rujiste. Klasnik was rather far away from Prelovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't true that Rujiste is near Klasnik, only three or four kilometres away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. Rujiste is closer to Prelovo than Klasnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know a teacher named Edina Bosno?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes, from Prelovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Are you sure she wasn't in Klasnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: She may have been, but she taught the children from Klasnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that the children in the machine school went to school at an opposite shift than you did in secondary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: There were two shifts, the first and the second. We saw each other. Sometimes we share the same shift, sometimes not, but we always saw each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, of the gentlemen that first came earlier in the day, you said that there was a young boy, tall and gangly. Did you recognise this boy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No, I did not. It was the first time I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I asked you if you recognised him, and at first you said yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. I said I did not recognise him. I keep saying that, that I did not know him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The transcript does have you answering that question with yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I said that I didn't know the youngest of them. I said that he was tall, thin, and the youngest of the group.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when Mitar Vasiljevic was seen at the beginning before you went to the Mahala neighbourhood, was he armed then as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, before that, you were being abused by police officers at the hotel. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How could you tell they were police officers versus other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Because policemen wore blue camouflage uniforms. It was police uniform -- it had been police uniform since before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the -- everyone at the hotel was wearing blue camouflage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. There were those in other coloured camouflage uniforms as well as the uniforms of the former JNA. There were several different types of uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can you estimate how many men and soldiers comprised this group of people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. There were many going in and out of the hotel, going up and down the street. I did not count them. I was in fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I'm not asking you to count them. I'm asking more of a round and rough estimate.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. All I know is that there were many. I don't know how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When Mitar Vasiljevic first approached your group, how close were you able to get to him, next to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: We were quite close, perhaps 10 to 20 metres. He came to the garden, stood in front of us and told us to go to Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you -- did he ever appear intoxicated or drunk?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Well, I do know he was an alcoholic. As to whether he was inebriated at that moment, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how had you heard that he was an alcoholic? Had you known that before that day, or did that come to your attention after that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. I used to see him at school -- at the school always drunk. His wife Milojka worked in a shop called Granap in Prelovo. He was always there, always drunk. That's how I used to see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When you describe someone as drunk -- I mean, some people will drink and they'll look fine. How would you describe appearing drunk?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I don't want to describe that. I'm not interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I'd ask you just to describe Mitar when he was drunk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid. Mr. Alarid, the cross-examination appears to be meandering and wandering.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, to be honest, Your Honour, I'm going through her prior testimony somewhat, and there were some references in the prior testimony, even though they didn't come out quite as much today. Of course I'm going through Mitar Vasiljevic's testimony, and there was some descriptions as to alcoholism and what-not, and I was just wondering. I'm sort of just moving backwards and hoping to finish relatively soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How soon?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When are we taking a break, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Probably a little bit after the break, but not that long. I don't think I'll go to the end of the evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, but be a bit more focused in the questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, how far -- how far away is the hotel from the square where you first encountered police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: It's right close to the square. The hotel is on the square.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And so was it the same police that you first encountered entering the square that were also at the hotel throwing insults at you and your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Some policemen were in front of the SUP. Another group of policemen awaited us in front of the hotel. I don't know whether it was the same people, though, or two completely different groups of policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you stated on direct examination that they were discussing where you should go, one of two options. Did it appear --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. They shouted at us, telling us to go to the Muslim houses there, and they were discussing amongst themselves where they should send us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did it appear that they knew you were coming, or was your arrival on the square a surprise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. To me, it appeared that they had known we would come. They seemed to wanted to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. Again just one intervention. In transcript I cannot see -- I think that witness mentioned location Bikavac, but I cannot see anywhere in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Was that in her last answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Before the last answer, before the last one. About the locations and options.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you mention Bikavac, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In relation to what? Would you just tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a neighbourhood called Bikavac in Visegrad close to the hotel. It is a neighbourhood of Visegrad called Bikavac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to take you back to the beginning of when this -- you left your village. Isn't true that it was actually a police officer that came to you in the village and told you all that you had to leave, threatening you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And was -- can you name that police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. His name is Radomir Djuric.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that Ilija Gavrilovic was also a police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Ilija went to Visegrad before we did with another person by the name of Dragomir Grujic. They took my relative's car and went there before we did. When we were at Greben, they told us, "You, the Turks, should move. You need to go to Visegrad, and no one is to leave it alive."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How did they come in possession of your relative's car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: They just took it. They came to the village and took the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when they took -- was this before they asked you to leave? Was this before the 13th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How long before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I don't remember how long before, but I do know for a fact that they seized it. Other than that, they would come to the village and cherry-picked our possessions, just take them over to their own houses under the pretext that they would be taking care of the stuff while we were away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, endeavour to finish by the break, which is at 25 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know who the chief of police was at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Drago Gavrilovic was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was he also a -- was he also a member --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was he also a member of the SDS party and the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when these people, these police were cherry-picking your possessions, how long had this been going on before you were forced from your homes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: It was not the policemen. It was our neighbours, Serbs, who would be taking our belongings, and it was throughout that day, the 13th of June, that they kept coming to our homes and taking stuff away back to their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And did this include Dragomir Gavrilovic? Drago, I mean.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. Dragomir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did it also include Drago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When they told you that they were -- you had to leave your homes, isn't it true that they told you it was other Serbs from nearby villages putting pressure? Is that what they told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes. They said that the Serbs from Prelovo were exerting pressure on them, that they would be coming to our village and that we could no longer stay there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when Ilija had taken the automobile from your cousin, had they given any receipt or confirmation that they had in fact taken the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No. No, nothing of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That would conclude my examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the only thing I would do as a final matter, although it doesn't require the witness, is that we introduce the witness's statement to the OTP, 21st of March, 2001, which has been uploaded as 1D10-1480, and the prior testimony of the -- trial testimony of the witness has been 1D10-1498.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You want to have those admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, they will become Exhibits number 1D36 and 1D37 respectively, both under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. No questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May I have one moment, Your Honour? May I have one moment? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Just a couple of questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Witness, you were asked about a person named Edina Bosno. Do you recall being asked about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And could you tell us again who this person is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: I heard that she was a teacher and that she resided in the village of Prelovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you know what school she taught at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you know if she taught any kids -- any children who came from Klasnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-101
utterances.text: She probably did, because she did not teach in Prelovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, that concludes your evidence. We thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it, and you may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, what is your position with witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, we had expected that this witness would take the majority of the day. The next witness is Mitar Vasiljevic. I know that Mr. Domazet was speaking with him all day today. I'm not sure if Mr. Domazet has concluded his discussions with him. I can attempt to check that over the break if Your Honour would wish to begin his evidence in the last session. I expect, Your Honour, that my examination -- actually, I know my examination will take an hour and a half, and I think we will be able to conclude it tomorrow and the next day, but I'll leave it to the Court as whether you want me to inquire whether he's available in the next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll stick to the schedule. We'll hear him tomorrow, in which case we are adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 10th day of September, 2008, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25
